deck.name: Curiosity Mix · Medium
deck.description: Unexpected facts across animals, inventions, language, history, science and games.

questions.prompt: Which planet takes longer to rotate once relative to the stars than to orbit the Sun?
questions.explanation: Venus's sidereal rotation takes about 243 Earth days; its orbit takes about 225.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: Two pump blood through the gills; the third supplies the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: Which mammal is known for producing cube-shaped droppings?
questions.explanation: Differences in the intestinal wall's elasticity help form the shapes.

questions.prompt: What is a shark's skeleton mainly made of?
questions.explanation: A shark?s internal skeleton is made mainly of cartilage rather than the bone found in most bony fish.

questions.prompt: What color is a polar bear's skin beneath its fur?
questions.explanation: The fur looks white, but the underlying skin is dark.

questions.prompt: Which of these is botanically classified as a berry?
questions.explanation: Botanical berries develop from a single ovary; everyday fruit names use different rules.

questions.prompt: Which plant family includes peanuts?
questions.explanation: Peanuts are related to beans and peas, despite the word nut in their name.

questions.prompt: What kind of plant is bamboo?
questions.explanation: Bamboo belongs to the grass family, Poaceae, despite its tree-like size and woody stems.

questions.prompt: What kingdom includes ordinary mushrooms?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms are fungi, a kingdom separate from plants and animals.

questions.prompt: What is rust commonly formed from?
choices: Copper reacting with nitrogen and oil
Silver reacting with carbon and salt
Iron reacting with oxygen and water
Aluminum reacting with hydrogen and wax
questions.explanation: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water, producing iron oxides.

questions.prompt: Which metal is liquid at ordinary room temperature?
questions.explanation: Gallium melts near 30 degrees Celsius, above an ordinary 20-25 degree room.

questions.prompt: Which mountain is tallest when measured above sea level?
questions.explanation: Measuring from a mountain's base gives a different comparison from measuring above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which canal is a sea-level waterway without navigation locks?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal uses locks to raise and lower ships.

questions.prompt: What is the world's largest desert by area?
questions.explanation: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, not by heat or sand.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra VII lived closer in time to which event?
choices: The building of the Great Pyramid
The founding of the first Egyptian dynasty
questions.explanation: Cleopatra died in 30 BCE; the Great Pyramid dates to roughly 2560 BCE, and Apollo 11 landed in 1969.

questions.prompt: Which company began in 1889 by making playing cards?
questions.explanation: Nintendo began in Kyoto in 1889 by producing hanafuda playing cards before expanding into games.

questions.prompt: The name LEGO comes from Danish words meaning what?
questions.explanation: The Danish phrase is leg godt.

questions.prompt: At what temperature do Celsius and Fahrenheit have the same numerical value?
questions.explanation: Substituting into F = 9C/5 + 32 gives -40 on both scales.

questions.prompt: Which chess piece can normally jump over other pieces?
questions.explanation: The knight moves in an L shape and can jump over intervening pieces, unlike the other chess pieces.

questions.prompt: How many points is Q worth in standard English-language Scrabble?
questions.explanation: Z is also worth ten points; letter values differ between language editions.

questions.prompt: Which electronic instrument is traditionally played without touching it?
questions.explanation: The performer's hands influence electromagnetic fields near its antennas.

questions.prompt: Who wrote The Divine Comedy?
questions.explanation: Dante Alighieri wrote The Divine Comedy, an Italian poem that follows a journey through the afterlife.

questions.prompt: Who wrote Around the World in Eighty Days?
questions.explanation: Jules Verne published Around the World in Eighty Days in 1872.

questions.prompt: What is Sherlock Holmes's famous London address?
questions.explanation: 221B Baker Street is the fictional London address associated with Sherlock Holmes.

questions.prompt: Which subject was not one of the five original Nobel Prize categories?
questions.explanation: The original categories were physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: She shared the 1903 physics prize and later won the 1911 chemistry prize.

questions.prompt: Which city is home to the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal stands in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the Yamuna River.

questions.prompt: Which sugar is part of DNA's backbone?
questions.explanation: RNA contains ribose instead of deoxyribose.

questions.prompt: What number does the Roman numeral M represent?
questions.explanation: M is the Roman numeral for one thousand.

questions.prompt: What does deuce mean in an ordinary tennis game?
questions.explanation: At deuce, both players have 40 points; one must win two consecutive points to take the game.

questions.prompt: Which containers served as the earliest basketball baskets?
questions.explanation: James Naismith developed basketball in 1891.

questions.prompt: Which type of joint is the human shoulder's main joint?
questions.explanation: The shoulder?s ball-and-socket joint allows movement in many directions, including rotation.

questions.prompt: Which process separates a liquid mixture using differences in boiling behavior?
questions.explanation: Distillation separates liquid mixtures by vaporizing components and condensing them, using their different boiling behavior.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's dry atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air.

questions.prompt: Which part of an egg contains most of its fat?
questions.explanation: The egg yolk contains most of an egg?s fat, while the white is mostly water and protein.

questions.prompt: Which common musical marking means to play softly?
questions.explanation: Piano is a dynamic instruction as well as the name of an instrument.

questions.prompt: Sound waves can travel through a perfect vacuum.
questions.explanation: Ordinary sound needs a medium such as air, water or a solid.

questions.prompt: Whales are mammals rather than fish.
questions.explanation: They breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.prompt: What is pareidolia?
questions.answer: Perceiving a recognizable image or pattern in something ambiguous, such as seeing a face in a cloud.
questions.explanation: Pareidolia is the tendency to perceive familiar patterns, such as faces, in ambiguous sights or sounds.

questions.prompt: What is bioluminescence?
questions.answer: Light produced by a chemical reaction in a living organism.
questions.explanation: Bioluminescence is light generated by chemical reactions within living organisms.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the Great Red Spot, a long-lived storm in its atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm observed in Jupiter’s atmosphere.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which light cannot escape?
questions.explanation: The event horizon marks the point beyond which no signal can escape the black hole.

questions.prompt: Which unit is used to measure the frequency of a sound wave?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz, or cycles per second.

questions.prompt: Which particle in an atom carries a positive electric charge?
questions.explanation: Protons have positive charge; electrons are negative and neutrons have no net charge.

questions.prompt: Which structure in a plant leaf allows much of its gas exchange?
questions.explanation: Stomata are small pores, usually on leaves, that regulate gas exchange and water loss.

questions.prompt: What do conifers such as pines usually produce instead of flowers?
questions.explanation: Conifers are gymnosperms that produce seeds in cones rather than flowers and fruits.

questions.prompt: Which organism is a single-celled prokaryote?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes: their cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which process turns atmospheric nitrogen into compounds plants can use?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing microbes convert nitrogen gas into biologically usable nitrogen compounds.

questions.prompt: Which ancient city was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE?
questions.explanation: The eruption of Vesuvius buried Pompeii and neighboring Roman settlements.

questions.prompt: Which civilization built the city of Tikal, now an archaeological site in Guatemala?
questions.explanation: Tikal was a major city of the ancient Maya civilization.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between the Arabian Peninsula and northeastern Africa?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea separates the Arabian Peninsula from northeastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Budapest?
questions.explanation: The Danube runs through Budapest, dividing the historic Buda and Pest sides of the city.

questions.prompt: Which country uses the yen as its currency?
questions.explanation: The yen is Japan’s national currency.

questions.prompt: Which language family includes Spanish, French, and Italian?
questions.explanation: These languages developed from Latin and belong to the Romance branch of Indo-European.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix “inter-” usually mean?
questions.explanation: Inter- appears in words such as international, meaning between or among nations.

questions.prompt: Which figure of speech gives a nonhuman thing human qualities?
questions.explanation: Personification describes an object or idea as if it had human traits.

questions.prompt: What does “bilingual” describe?
questions.explanation: Bilingual commonly describes a person or community that uses two languages.

questions.prompt: Which printing technology did Johannes Gutenberg help popularize in Europe?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg’s mid-fifteenth-century press used reusable movable metal type.

questions.prompt: Who developed the first widely used inactivated polio vaccine?
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk developed an inactivated polio vaccine that was licensed in the United States in 1955.

questions.prompt: Which art term describes a strong contrast between light and dark?
questions.explanation: Chiaroscuro is the use of light and shadow to create volume and dramatic contrast.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.prompt: What is the process called when water vapor changes directly into ice without first becoming liquid?
questions.explanation: Deposition is a gas-to-solid phase change, such as frost forming from water vapor.

questions.prompt: Which type of rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form when heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids alter existing rock.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a lighthouse?
choices: To measure rainfall and wind along a coast
To mark the boundary between time zones
To track earthquakes and warn of tsunamis
To help guide and warn ships near coasts
questions.explanation: Lighthouses provide a visible navigational aid and warning near hazards or harbors.

questions.prompt: Which board game objective is to connect two opposite sides of a hexagonal grid?
questions.explanation: In Hex, players try to form an unbroken path between their assigned opposite sides.

questions.prompt: In golf, what is one stroke under par on a hole called?
questions.explanation: A birdie is a score of one stroke below the hole’s par.

questions.prompt: How many players from one side are on court in standard doubles badminton?
questions.explanation: Doubles badminton is played by two players on each side of the net.

questions.prompt: Which food is made by fermenting cabbage with lactic-acid bacteria?
questions.explanation: Sauerkraut is fermented cabbage; lactic-acid bacteria help preserve it and create its tangy flavor.

questions.prompt: Which spice comes from the dried stigmas of a crocus flower?
questions.explanation: Saffron consists of the dried stigmas of Crocus sativus flowers.

questions.prompt: What does an insulator do in an electrical circuit?
choices: Resists the flow of electric charge
questions.explanation: An electrical insulator strongly resists charge flow, unlike a conductor.

questions.prompt: Which scientist is associated with the laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation: Kepler formulated three mathematical laws describing how planets orbit the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which ancient writing material was made from a plant that grew along the Nile?
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptians made papyrus sheets from the pith of the papyrus plant.

questions.prompt: Which ocean current helps keep western Europe milder than some regions at similar latitudes?
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic Current transports relatively warm water toward western Europe.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a word formed from the initial letters of a phrase and pronounced as a word?
questions.explanation: NATO is an acronym because its initial letters are pronounced together as a word.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the largest volcano known in the solar system, Olympus Mons?
questions.explanation: Olympus Mons is a shield volcano on Mars.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the boundary where two tectonic plates move apart?
questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, tectonic plates move away from each other and new crust can form.

questions.prompt: Which part of a camera controls how long light reaches the sensor?
questions.explanation: The shutter controls exposure time by determining how long light reaches the sensor or film.

questions.prompt: Which gas is used by many plants during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and use carbon atoms to build sugars during photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which international organization publishes the World Heritage List?
questions.explanation: UNESCO’s World Heritage Centre coordinates the World Heritage List and Convention.

questions.prompt: Which composer wrote the ballet The Nutcracker?
questions.explanation: Tchaikovsky composed the ballet The Nutcracker, first performed in 1892.

questions.prompt: Which sport features a scrum as a method of restarting play?
questions.explanation: A scrum is a set-piece restart used in rugby union after certain minor infringements.

questions.prompt: Which ocean borders the east coast of the United States?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic Ocean lies to the east of the contiguous United States.

questions.prompt: What does a cartographer make?
questions.explanation: Cartography is the practice of making and studying maps.

questions.prompt: Which nutrient is the body’s primary quick source of energy?
questions.explanation: The body breaks many carbohydrates into glucose, an important energy source for cells.

questions.prompt: A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon.
questions.explanation: Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon during a lunar eclipse.

questions.prompt: The human liver is part of the digestive system.
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile and performs other functions that support digestion and metabolism.

questions.prompt: A pH below 7 is acidic in the usual aqueous pH scale.
questions.explanation: At about room temperature, neutral aqueous solutions are near pH 7; lower values are acidic.

questions.prompt: All metals are magnetic at room temperature.
questions.explanation: Only some materials, including iron, cobalt, and nickel, are strongly ferromagnetic at room temperature.

questions.prompt: An anagram is made by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase.
questions.explanation: For example, listen and silent use the same letters in a different order.

questions.prompt: Earth’s tectonic plates are completely stationary.
questions.explanation: Tectonic plates move slowly over geological time.

questions.prompt: A light-year is a unit of time.
questions.explanation: A light-year measures distance: how far light travels in one year.

questions.prompt: What does “etymology” study?
questions.answer: The origins and historical development of words.
questions.explanation: Etymologists trace how a word’s form and meaning change over time.

questions.prompt: What is a sonnet?
questions.answer: A fourteen-line poem with a structured rhyme scheme and meter.
questions.explanation: Different sonnet traditions use different rhyme schemes, including the Shakespearean and Petrarchan forms.

questions.prompt: What is an eclipse?
questions.answer: An event in which one celestial body moves into the shadow of another or blocks its light from an observer.
questions.explanation: Solar and lunar eclipses occur when the Sun, Earth, and Moon align in particular ways.

questions.prompt: What is a catalyst?
questions.answer: A substance that speeds a chemical reaction without being consumed overall.
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

questions.prompt: Which element has atomic number 1?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has one proton, so its atomic number is 1.

questions.prompt: What is the atomic number of hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Atomic number counts protons; every hydrogen nucleus has one proton.

questions.prompt: Which scale ranks minerals by their resistance to scratching?
questions.explanation: The Mohs scale compares relative mineral hardness by testing which minerals can scratch others.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish artist painted The Persistence of Memory?
questions.explanation: Salvador Dali painted the 1931 surrealist work known for its melting clocks.

questions.prompt: In musical notation, what does the dynamic marking “piano” instruct a performer to do?
questions.explanation: The Italian word piano means soft; pianissimo (pp) means very soft.
